_comment: XC-3 Phase 0b ledger of every src/app/api/**/route.ts that imports the RLS-bypassing service-role client (@/lib/supabase-admin or a relative path to lib/supabase-admin). This list RATCHETS DOWN ONLY: as Phase 2/3 migrate read routes onto the RLS-scoped supabase-server client, their entries are pruned here in the same PR. A NEW admin-importing route that is absent from this ledger FAILS src/__tests__/api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts (which re-derives the detected set from source with the same import matcher). 263 -> 264: GenAI Phase 5a outcome-prediction cross-student read (service-role after canAccessStudent). 264 -> 265 (2026-07-29, architect-reviewed): P0-1 quota display/enforcement gap — src/app/api/usage/daily/route.ts reads the caller's OWN daily quota from get_plan_limit(), the SAME authority check_and_record_usage() enforces from. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: migration 20260729130400 §5 (re-asserting 20260516040000/20260516050000) REVOKEs EXECUTE ON public.get_plan_limit(uuid, text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, so an RLS-scoped session cannot call it at all. Bounded surface: one STABLE read-only RPC + one own-row SELECT on student_daily_usage, both keyed on the SESSION-derived auth.studentId (students.auth_user_id = caller) — no studentId is ever accepted from the request, so there is no cross-student path. Read-only: no insert/update/increment/grant; the hard gate stays checkAndIncrementQuota -> check_and_record_usage in /api/foxy. Gated by authorizeRequest() on 'foxy.chat'/'quiz.attempt' (both granted to the student role by 20260612123200); EVERY unrecognised ?feature= — inherited Object.prototype keys (toString/constructor/valueOf/hasOwnProperty/__proto__/isPrototypeOf/propertyIsEnumerable/toLocaleString) included — is rejected 400 BEFORE authorizeRequest and before any service-role call. Architect-verified against shipped source 2026-07-29: FEATURE_PERMISSION is a new Map<string, string> (route.ts:82-85) and the guard is typeof permission !== 'string' (route.ts:95-100); Map.prototype.get consults no prototype chain, so inherited keys are unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard each new call site must remember, and no caller-controlled string can reach get_plan_limit's generous ai_calls_total ELSE arm. HISTORY (CLOSED — recorded so the fix is not re-litigated, not as an open item): the pre-ship draft used a plain object literal typed Record<string, string>, where inherited keys returned truthy and slipped past the !permission guard. The impact was BROADER than first recorded here: a student caller got an unhandled 500 (rbac.ts:785 calls .split() on the non-string permission in the deny branch, above the try), but a super_admin caller took the isSuperAdmin short-circuit at rbac.ts:779-780, which skips the permission check entirely, so a prototype key DID reach get_plan_limit and land in its ai_calls_total ELSE arm. That path additionally required the caller to own a student row, and get_plan_limit is a read-only STABLE function, so the over-generous number was DISPLAY-only and never raised the ENFORCED cap in check_and_record_usage. Both paths are closed by the Map plus typeof guard, pinned by 4 tests covering 8 prototype keys. Response is 4 ints + 1 bool, no PII (P13). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER wrapper get_my_plan_limit(p_feature text) GRANTed to authenticated, move the route to the RLS-scoped client, and prune this entry. Do NOT instead GRANT EXECUTE on get_plan_limit(uuid, text) to authenticated — it takes p_student_id and performs no auth.uid() check, so that would expose every student's cap to every authenticated user. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 268 -> 269 (2026-08-02, architect-reviewed): Mock Exam Runner v2 autosave — new save-only route src/app/api/exams/papers/[id]/autosave/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: mock_test_attempts RLS (20260520000008) keys mock_test_attempts_update_own/select_own on student_id = auth.uid() directly (student_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)), but this entire route family — this route's already-ledgered siblings [id]/start/route.ts and [id]/submit/route.ts (see 'Phase 2.2 mock-exam remediation' above) — resolves and filters on authorizeRequest()'s studentId, which is students.id, a DIFFERENT uuid than auth.uid(). An RLS-scoped client (supabase-server/supabase-route) filtering .eq('student_id', studentId) with that same studentId would be silently zero-rowed by the auth.uid()-keyed policy — indistinguishable from the route's own legitimate persisted:false no-op branch, i.e. a silent persistence failure, not a security win. Bounded surface: a single UPDATE scoped to id + student_id + exam_paper_id + status='in_progress', touching only the pre-existing client_metadata jsonb column — NEVER score_percent/raw_score/xp_earned/status/submitted_at (enforced by the route's own field-level write shape, not by a WHERE filter). Gated by the same exam.view authorizeRequest() permission as all three siblings; student_id/exam_paper_id/status are app-supplied filters only, never derived from a request-controlled join, so there is no cross-student read/write path. RATCHET-DOWN PATH: reconcile student_id semantics across the whole [id]/{start,submit,autosave} family (store auth.uid() consistently, matching the table's own RLS design, or add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER autosave RPC mirroring submit_mock_test_attempt), then move all three routes to the RLS-scoped client together — flagged for architect/backend follow-up, out of scope for this PR. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-03, architect-approved in the P1 verifyCronAuth batch): src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts DELETED — it was a deprecated alias for /api/cron/daily-cron, scheduled by nothing and carrying only deprecation telemetry; its entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 265 (2026-08-03, P2-7b): teacher/messages/{route,threads,threads/[id]/messages} migrated to SECURITY DEFINER RPCs under RLS (createSupabaseServerClient), pruned in the same change so the ledger ratchets DOWN. 268 -> 269 (2026-08-05, Foxy North-Star Phase 5 lane U10): NEW route src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/me/route.ts legitimately uses the admin client. Service-role read of the get_leaderboard_percentile RPC scoped to the SESSION-derived studentId (auth.uid()-resolved; ?student_id ignored) after authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view'); returns caller-owned percentile band + PII-free neighbours. Ratchet-down path: replace with an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC then move to the RLS-scoped client. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-06, P1 health consolidation, commit eaa7e1ab): src/app/api/health/route.ts migrated to a pure-liveness endpoint (no downstream dependency probes, no service-role reads) and its ledger entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 267 (2026-08-10): src/app/api/v2/student/profile/route.ts migrated to the RLS-scoped request client (createSupabaseRouteClient) behind the new learners repository module; own-row read is served by the students_select_merged policy (auth_user_id = auth.uid()), so service-role is no longer required. Pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN. 267 -> 269 (2026-08-11, leaderboard SEV1 Pattern-B repair): TWO new routes legitimately require service-role. (a) src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/titles/route.ts — student_titles has RLS ENABLED with EXACTLY ONE policy, "Service role full access on student_titles" (baseline :20003); there is NO student SELECT policy at all, so an RLS-scoped client reads 0 rows for every caller and the "My Titles" tab was permanently empty. Bounded surface: one SELECT on student_titles filtered .eq(student_id, auth.studentId) — the SESSION-derived id; a ?student_id param is ignored. Own-data only, no cross-student path. (b) src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/streaks/route.ts — a peer streak leaderboard; challenge_streaks RLS is own-row-only (challenge_streaks_student_select, baseline :20607) and students_select_merged is own/teacher-of/guardian-of, so a cross-student board is structurally impossible under RLS (the page previously read it from the BROWSER and rendered the single returned row as a "Top Streaks" board). Bounded surface: two capped SELECTs (challenge_streaks >= visibility threshold, then students by id IN the surviving set), projected through an explicit P13 whitelist — peers get rank/student_id/name/grade/current_streak plus badges already implied by the exposed current_streak; best_streak, avatar_url, school, city, last_challenge_date and the mercy-day counters never leave the server. Gated by authorizeRequest(leaderboard.view) / (progress.view_own for titles). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (get_my_titles(), get_streak_leaderboard(p_limit)) GRANTed to authenticated, mirroring get_class_leaderboard, then move both routes to the RLS-scoped client and prune these entries. NOTE the sibling src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/my-class/route.ts added in the same change is deliberately NOT here: it uses the RLS-scoped createSupabaseRouteClient (class_students own-enrollment policy + the already-SECURITY-DEFINER get_class_leaderboard RPC granted to authenticated). 269 -> 270 (2026-08-11, support first-response SLA): NEW route src/app/api/internal/admin/support/metrics/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience, and the RLS-scoped alternative was checked FIRST and rejected on evidence: NEITHER table this route reads has ANY operator/admin/support-role SELECT policy. support_tickets has exactly two SELECT policies, both requester-anchored -- 'Users can read own tickets' (email = the caller's own auth.users email OR student_id IN the caller's own students, baseline :20262) and support_tickets_self_select (student_id IN own students, baseline :22378). support_ticket_replies (20260814000012) has exactly three policies: _owner_select (authenticated, is_internal=false AND own student-filed ticket), _owner_insert, and _service_role_all; that migration's own policy comment states the design explicitly -- 'Operator replies, internal notes, edits and redactions all go through the service-role client, which bypasses RLS. Authorisation for those writes is enforced in the route by authorizeAdmin()/authorizeRequest(), NOT here.' So an operator holding support.view_tickets, reading through createSupabaseRouteClient, would see ONLY the tickets that operator personally filed. The failure mode is the reason this is disqualifying rather than merely degraded: this route exists to make the newly-published 2-business-day SLA falsifiable, and over a near-empty row set it would return breach_count 0 and meeting_promise true -- i.e. it would silently certify that we are meeting the promise PRECISELY BECAUSE it cannot see the breaches. A metric that fails toward 'all clear' is worse than no metric. The RLS-scoped client is therefore not a second line of defense here, it is a silent-zero. Consistency: the sibling operator console src/app/api/internal/admin/support/route.ts (ticket list, thread view, status PATCH, operator reply POST) is already in this ledger, reads the SAME two tables, and is gated by the SAME authorizeRequest('support.view_tickets') code; splitting one operator surface across two clients would buy nothing. BOUNDED SURFACE: read-only, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/RPC of any kind. Exactly three query shapes, all hard-capped -- (1) support_tickets created inside a 1..365-day window, LIMIT 5000; (2) still-open support_tickets of any age, LIMIT 2000; (3) support_ticket_replies chunked by ticket_id IN (<=200) with is_internal=false AND author_role IN (operator,admin,system), for the ticket ids returned by (1)+(2) only. Both query params (days, queue_limit) are Number.parseInt + clamped to fixed ranges before use; no caller-supplied string reaches any filter, and there is no id/tenant parameter at all, so there is no cross-tenant or request-steered read path. P13 FIELD WHITELIST (the load-bearing justification): support_tickets carries email, user_name, subject, message, device_info and admin_notes -- NONE is selected. The ticket SELECT list is pinned to the single TICKET_COLUMNS constant 'id, category, status, created_at, resolved_at' and the reply SELECT to 'ticket_id, created_at, author_role'. No message body and no author identity (no author_user_id, no author name) is ever read, so no reply text can reach the response even by accident. The response is aggregate counts/percentiles plus a work queue of (ticket_id, category, status, created_at, age); ticket UUIDs only. Errors return a generic 'Internal error' body rather than the PostgREST string, which would otherwise echo the ticket-id IN-list back to the caller. Nothing is logged and nothing is written to audit_logs -- read-only aggregate, no operator action to audit. RATCHET-DOWN PATH (concrete): add a SECURITY DEFINER RPC public.get_support_first_response_metrics(p_days int, p_queue_limit int) RETURNS jsonb that opens with IF NOT public.check_permission(auth.uid(), 'support.view_tickets') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION -- check_permission(uuid, text) already exists SECURITY DEFINER in the baseline (:1973) and resolves user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions with is_active/expires_at honoured -- projects the same five ticket columns and three reply columns, and is GRANTed EXECUTE to authenticated with EXECUTE REVOKEd from PUBLIC/anon; then move this route to createSupabaseRouteClient and prune this entry. IMPORTANT: the support_ticket_first_response view whose DDL is handed to architect in this route's header comment does NOT achieve that ratchet-down and must not be mistaken for it -- it is declared security_invoker = true and GRANTed to service_role ONLY, so reading it still requires this admin client; it is an ad-hoc-SQL convenience for ops, not the migration path. Do NOT instead add an operator SELECT policy to support_tickets: that would widen RLS over the whole row including email/user_name/subject/message/device_info/admin_notes, trading a narrow server-side column whitelist for broad table-level PII exposure (P13 regression). The RPC keeps the projection server-side where it already is. 270 -> 271 (2026-08-15, architect-reviewed): curated-corpus signed-URL minting — NEW route src/app/api/learning-sources/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: the `learning-sources` storage bucket is PRIVATE with ZERO storage.objects policies BY DESIGN (migration 20260816000001_learning_sources_bucket.sql — the documented house convention established for school-invoices in 20260507130001: with no policy, RLS on storage.objects denies anon and authenticated by default and only the service role, which bypasses RLS, can read), so an RLS-scoped client structurally CANNOT mint a signed URL for any object in the bucket; there is no per-user storage policy to lean on. Bounded surface: read-only — a single createSignedUrl call with TTL 300s (5 minutes), no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/RPC. The route is gated by authorizeRequest() BEFORE any service-role call and validates the content-addressed path shape ({board}/{grade}/{subject_code}/{sha256_16}/{filename}: hex sha256 >= 16 chars, grade 6-12, 2-8-char subject code, whitelisted extensions pdf/json/png/jpg/jpeg, and a filename ban on '/', '\' and '..' so no traversal outside the convention). Response is signed URL + path + TTL only — no PII (P13). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: none via storage RLS — the bucket migration explicitly forbids resolving this with a permissive storage.objects policy ('Do NOT fix the missing policies by adding a permissive one'), because the bucket holds rights-restricted third-party PDFs; this route is the permanent sanctioned signed-URL read path for the private bucket, mirroring the safeguarding-lane service-role-only-by-design precedent. 271 -> 272 (2026-08-11, architect-reviewed, recorded 2026-08-23 during b00b9c872 reconciliation): Phase 4 quiz session resume — NEW route src/app/api/quiz/session/[sessionId]/progress/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: public.quiz_session_shuffles has RLS ENABLED with exactly THREE policies and ALL THREE are FOR SELECT (student/parent/teacher) — there is NO INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy at all, and migration 20260814000020 made that denial explicit at the privilege layer too (post-condition 4d asserts `authenticated` retains no write privilege). An RLS-scoped client issuing this route's UPDATE would therefore be silently zero-rowed — indistinguishable from the route's own legitimate first-write-wins 'saved:false' no-op branch, i.e. a silent durability failure, not a security win. Bounded surface: ONE table (quiz_session_shuffles), ONE write verb (UPDATE) touching only student_selected_displayed_index / student_time_spent_seconds / student_answered_at (20260802130000) and session_mode (20260814000021) — NEVER shuffle_map, options_snapshot, correct_answer_index_snapshot, integrity_hash or options_version_at_serve. Auth gate: requireOwnedSession() runs authorizeRequest(request, 'quiz.attempt') FIRST, then an owner-vs-session studentId probe (404 unknown, 403 mismatch); no student id is ever accepted from the request body. Full justification in apps/host/src/__tests__/api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts's own history log (Phase 4 quiz session resume entry). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER persist_quiz_answer_progress RPC, after which the route moves to the RLS-scoped client and this entry is pruned. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 272 -> 273 (2026-08-11, architect-reviewed, recorded 2026-08-23 during b00b9c872 reconciliation): teacher worksheet answer key — NEW route src/app/api/teacher/worksheets/answer-key/route.ts, created expressly to UNBLOCK the question_bank answer-key column ACL. Service-role is REQUIRED, not convenient: public.question_bank.correct_answer_index is today SELECTable by every signed-in user (students, parents and teachers all authenticate as the SAME `authenticated` Postgres role), so neither RLS nor a column ACL can distinguish 'teacher printing an answer key' from 'student reading the key mid-quiz' — the widest answer-key leak in the product. Bounded surface: ONE table, ONE verb (SELECT), READ-ONLY, over exactly six columns, filtered on subject + grade + is_active = true (+ optional difficulty), LIMITed to count*3 with count validated to an integer in [1,30]. Auth gate: authorizeRequest(request, 'worksheet.create') runs FIRST (an EXISTING permission already granted to the teacher role by 20260612123200 — no new RBAC migration), plus a SECOND content-side gate (resolveTeacherContentScope) restricting the read to (subject, grade) pairs the caller actually teaches, failing closed on an empty scope. Full justification in apps/host/src/__tests__/api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts's own history log (269 -> 270, 2026-08-11 entry). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER get_worksheet_answer_key RPC, after which the route moves to the RLS-scoped client and this entry is pruned. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 273 -> 274 (recorded 2026-08-23, architect-reviewed during b00b9c872 reconciliation — NOT yet independently reviewed by ai-engineer/backend, flagged for follow-up): NEW route src/app/api/foxy/feedback/dimension/route.ts (Phase A.2 dimension-level Foxy feedback, untracked/in-flight at time of recording). Bounded surface as read from source: POST-only, gated by authorizeRequest(request, 'progress.view_own', { requireStudentId: true }) BEFORE any DB access; performs an explicit ownership check (SELECT id, student_id, role FROM foxy_chat_messages WHERE id = messageId, then verifies student_id === caller's own studentId AND role === 'assistant', collapsing 'not found' and 'wrong owner' into the same 404 so the route cannot be used to probe other students' message UUIDs) BEFORE invoking the record_message_dimension_feedback RPC — the route's own header comment states the RPC's auth.uid() guard does not fire under a service-role JWT, so this ownership check is the actual trust boundary. dimension is validated against a 4-value allowlist; reason is length-capped and never logged (P13). Service-role usage appears justified by the same pattern as sibling /api/foxy/feedback, but this entry is recorded provisionally — ai-engineer (Foxy feature owner) and backend should confirm the RPC's own grants/RLS posture and formalize or prune this entry in a follow-up. NOTE (recorded 2026-08-23, during the b00b9c872 reconciliation): src/app/api/v2/student/profile/route.ts was ALSO reverted by commit b00b9c872 from its 2026-08-10 RLS-scoped createSupabaseRouteClient migration (see the 268 -> 267 entry above) back to the pre-migration getSupabaseAdmin()-based implementation, as an unrelated side effect of that stale-base merge. Unlike the other reverted files documented here, this regression was independently found and fixed (route restored to createSupabaseRouteClient) by another agent during the SAME reconciliation window, before this ledger was committed — so this entry never needed a permanent allowlist row and the count sequence below does not pass through it. Recorded here only so the incident is not lost: if this route is EVER found importing supabase-admin again, that is this exact regression recurring, not a new legitimate use. 274 -> 275 (2026-08-23, architect-reviewed): Phase A.3 AI quality dashboard — NEW route src/app/api/super-admin/ai-quality/route.ts. Service-role is justified by the same super-admin-by-design pattern as the already-ledgered siblings foxy-quality/route.ts and foxy-report/[studentId]/route.ts: a read-only, cross-student aggregate over 5 tables (foxy_quality_scores, ops_events filtered to category='ai', foxy_message_feedback, foxy_message_dimension_feedback, foxy_chat_messages) over the trailing 30 days, feeding the AiQualityData contract consumed by super-admin/ai-quality/page.tsx. No RLS-scoped client can serve this: the read spans ALL students, not the caller's own row, so there is no per-user policy to lean on. Gated by authorizeRequest(request, 'super_admin.access') — the SAME existing permission the sibling routes use; no new RBAC. Read-only, no writes/RPCs. Response is counts/averages/enum-like keys (dimension names, coach modes, judge model/rubric version strings) only — never message text, `reason` free text, or student identifiers (P13). 273 -> 274 (2026-09-03): NEW route src/app/api/cron/expire-abandoned-checkouts/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED, not convenience: this is a cron job with no user session at all, exactly matching the existing ledgered sibling cron routes (expired-subscriptions, reconcile-payments, payments-health) which all use service-role for the identical reason — there is no auth.uid() to scope an RLS-scoped client to. Bounded surface: the route performs NO direct table reads/writes itself; its only DB interaction is a single call to the SECURITY DEFINER RPC expire_abandoned_checkout_attempts() (migration 20260903090000), which moves payment_history/student_subscriptions rows still 'pending' after a 72-hour window to a terminal status. P11 fix — see that migration's header for full context (a single abandoned checkout attempt generated 4,727 false payments-health alert events over 46 days with nothing in the codebase ever closing out an abandoned 'pending' row). 274 -> 271 (2026-09-05, Gate-2 D1 super-admin cleanup): src/app/api/super-admin/reconciliation/{route,[id]/approve/route,[id]/reject/route}.ts DELETED (confirmed zero real callers per docs/runbooks/super-admin-orphaned-apis.md's 'Delete in Phase 2' disposition, superseded by the live payment-ops/reconcile route) -- their 3 entries are pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. The 2 new routes added in the same PR, src/app/api/super-admin/announcements/{route,[id]/route}.ts, are deliberately NOT ledgered here: they use the RLS-scoped createSupabaseServerClient, not service-role -- admin_announcements' existing RLS (is_admin()-gated writes, baseline migration) already matches their exact access shape, so service-role was never genuinely required. 271 -> 272 (2026-09-05, Gate-2 Phase C global search): NEW route src/app/api/search/route.ts (super-admin-only for now -- see the route's own header for why per-role tenant-scoped search is deliberately deferred). Service-role is REQUIRED, not convenience: a cross-tenant search must see every school's students/teachers/schools, and RLS on those tables is own-row/own-school scoped, so an RLS-scoped client would silently zero-row a cross-tenant super-admin query. Same 'super-admin-by-design' justification as the already-ledgered siblings ai-quality/route.ts, foxy-report/[studentId]/route.ts, and synthesis-health/route.ts. Gated by authorizeRequest(request, 'super_admin.access') -- the SAME existing permission those siblings use; no new RBAC. Column projections are an explicit narrow allowlist per entity (P13/P-01 precedent, matching api/super-admin/users/route.ts) -- search results are compact identifiers for navigation, never a full record dump.
